mismatches.explanation: Java TypeUtil.project constructs a partial schema with default ID 0; Rust intentionally retains the source schema ID

Java ManifestReader filters eq-99.parquet using y < 20 and its writer-produced bounds; Rust process_delete_manifest_entry filters partitions only, so it indexes and attaches both eq-10.parquet and eq-99.parquet. This is an existing planning difference, with counters reflecting the different plans, not a normalization.

Both index two equality deletes. Java DeleteFileIndex.canContainEqDeletesForFile uses bounds to attach eq-10 only to written-10 and eq-99 to neither file. Rust uses partition and sequence checks, attaching both deletes to both files. The report counts actual attachments (Java 1, Rust 4).

Java TypeUtil.getProjectedIds includes the selected struct and its child ID; Rust reports the resolved top-level task projection. Both plan the whole struct. Nested report representation remains a contract decision for review.

Close-time counters include work ahead of consumption. Rust's concurrent entry workers can plan buffered tasks that Java's single-manifest iterator has not visited. Both reports are partial; this observed difference is retained, not normalized.
